il_g_worms_way.blurb: Worms Way is a cliffline sector within the Holy Boulders in Jackson County, southern Illinois, holding 17 boulder problems on sandstone. The grades stretch widely: roughly ten are easy to moderate, between V1 and V3, which makes it a handy stop for newer boulderers, while the rest climb through V5, V8 and into double digits, topping out near V12. The namesake line is a well-known hard test piece, and its much easier stand-start version is a popular classic. To find the wall, walk to the Shadow of a Man boulder and head to the cliffline facing it, then look for an angling jug feature.

il_a_the_ferne_clyffe_wall.blurb: A bolted sandstone wall inside Ferne Clyffe State Park, close to Goreville in southern Illinois, known locally as the Pump Wall. It holds 17 sport routes, with a lot of the climbing sitting between 5.9 and 5.10d: three at 5.9, eleven in the 5.10 range, a couple of 5.11s and one easy 5.6 warm-up. The lines are long and sustained, and the wall suits climbers stepping up from the gym to moderate outdoor leads. It is the first wall reached on the hike in from the lot, set behind big boulders, and it draws crowds on weekends.

il_a_starting_area.blurb: The Starting Area is the first bouldering zone at Lehigh Park, a small and little-visited spot near Oglesby in north-central Illinois. It has 17 problems, nearly all of them one boulder problem each, with one top-rope line mixed in. Most are low in grade, running from VB-V0 up to about V3, plus a single far harder entry, so it suits beginners and warm-ups more than projecting. Expect modest, sometimes loose local rock. Trails in the park are shared with mountain bikers, and in warm months the paths get buggy and overgrown with brush.
